items.title: Grayscale's Zcash ETF Marks Privacy Coin Breakthrough
points: Grayscale launched the first Zcash spot ETF Tuesday, offering regulated brokerage investors direct exposure to ZEC (the privacy coin that uses zero-knowledge proofs—cryptographic methods that prove something is true without revealing details).
The fund is positioned as a 'focused, higher-risk satellite position' for investors diversifying beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum.
Zcash surged to an 8-year high above $880, with open interest in perpetual futures (leveraged contracts that track the asset's price) reaching $1.8 billion.

The ETF approval arrives after Zcash deployed the Ironwood upgrade to patch a years-old vulnerability in its Orchard shielded pool; privacy features made it cryptographically impossible to determine whether the flaw had been exploited.

items.title: Treasury Launches Secondary Sanctions on Iran's Financial System
points: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled 'Operation Economic Outcast,' imposing secondary sanctions (penalties against entities that do business with sanctioned countries) on entities providing financial cover to Iran.
Digital assets were named among five target sectors, alongside technology, gold, aviation, and shipping.
Bessent argued 'total financial isolation' could reduce need for military action; prediction markets show only 8% probability of an Iran announcement by August 31.

items.title: Institutional Crypto Infrastructure Expansion
points: Franklin Templeton, managing $1.8 trillion in assets, deployed its tokenized treasury fund (a blockchain-based money market fund holding short-term government bonds) on Hong Kong exchange HashKey's Earn channel.

Coinbase launched tokenized stocks on Base, its Ethereum Layer 2 network (a blockchain that processes transactions faster than the main network), with tokens representing shares held by regulated custodian Alpaca, usable in decentralized finance (DeFi) applications that replicate traditional financial services on blockchain without intermediaries.
These developments signal growing institutional demand for bridging traditional finance and blockchain infrastructure.

items.title: Bitcoin Rally Amid Dollar Weakness
points: Bitcoin traded near $79,085 amid broader macro uncertainty, with the rally reflecting weakness in the U.S. dollar.
Concerns over Treasury bond buybacks are contributing to the uncertain macro backdrop.

items.title: Bitcoin Ad in Wall Street Journal Signals Mainstream Shift
points: A full-page Bitcoin advertisement ran in The Wall Street Journal, seen as a sign of mainstream financial media acceptance.
The ad marks what the newsletter calls Bitcoin's transition from a fringe asset to one under institutional consideration.

items.title: Analysts See Further Bitcoin Upside
points: Analysts project additional upside potential for Bitcoin price despite recent gains, suggesting more room for appreciation in the current market cycle.

sections.title: Treasury Launches Secondary Sanctions on Iran's Financial System

Bessent argued 'total financial isolation' could reduce need for military action, but traders interpret the move as adding pressure rather than replacing it; prediction markets show only 8% probability of Iran announcement by August 31.

sections.title: Institutional Crypto Infrastructure Expansion

These developments signal growing demand for bridging traditional finance and blockchain infrastructure among large institutions.
